# SCALAR · Algebraic Quantum Scalar Fields

Run:

```bash
python -m venv .venv
source .venv/bin/activate        # Windows: .venv\Scripts\activate
pip install -r requirements_scalar.txt
python scalar_app.py
```

Then open `http://127.0.0.1:8050`.


## Live surfaces

- Public app: https://heart-eagle-blade-hazel.grok.me
- Notion child page: https://app.notion.com/p/3d746094fd3081a9b279d3904123f8b4

- Reference certificate: `MC-AQSFT-E47-20260825`

## Computational spine

- `V = V_2^{\otimes3}`, dimension 125
- `C = J_tot^2`
- `K = (C-6I)(C-30I)`
- `E47 = ker K = E_6 \oplus E_30`, dimension 47
- `P47` is built from the actual Casimir eigenspaces
- `Omega_c = Tr(P47)/125 = 47/125`
- `Gamma_epsilon = I - epsilon K^2`
- default `epsilon = 1/99144`

## Scalar visualization lift

The app defines `L = -Delta` and assigns every algebraic Casimir component
a plane wave whose wavevector satisfies `|k|^2 = lambda`.

Therefore the terminal E47 visualization contains only the `lambda=6` and
`lambda=30` shells and satisfies

`(L-6)(L-30) phi = 0`

term-by-term.

This plane-wave construction is an explicit visualization map from the finite
algebra. It does not by itself identify a unique physical spacetime field.
